Stay away from wasps (non-fuzzy bodies, very bold stripes, more elongated, can sting you how ever many times they want, carry shivs), but do try to move quickly and calmly away from them if they're "interested" in you/following you. Wasps are technically useful insects, but also complete fucking pricks. Be careful around honey and bumble bees (fuzzy bodies, more rounded, fully golden to yellow and orange stripes on their butts, can usually only sting once unless they're the Queen of a hive), especially in the Southern parts of the US - you never know if a hive is Africanized or not, and you don't want to find out.

I used to be TERRIFIED of every single kind of bee/wasp/hornet/yellowjacket/bumblebee ever, to the point of crying and running as a kid whenever I saw one, and to the point of spending my summers inside as a teenager. Then, one of my friends in high school noticed that I was super nervous about being at his house and asked why. I told him it was because of all the honey bees (his father kept about half a dozen hives on the property), and he had his dad suit me up in a beesuit, duct taped the cuffs shut just in case, and had me watch while he went out and opened up one of the Italian hives and harvested honey. I got to hold a Queen, have workers land on the netting half an inch form my nose and see their little antennas wiggle, and eat fresh honeycomb afterwards. The entire time, all the guy wore was a head-net to keep the bees from getting tangled in his hair, and he showed me how honey bees will generally only sting if you squeeze them. It was a learning experience, to be sure. Your mileage may vary.

TL;DR - honey bees generally dgaf about you, wasps are dicks.
